summary: Migrate all use cases to CQRS with MediatR, Campaigns module with optimistic concurrency, Result Pattern, and unit tests.

briefBlocks.text: Sprint 2 — Campaigns, CQRS, MediatR & Unit Testing

briefBlocks.markdown: **DonationHub** is a donation management and crowdfunding platform that you build step by step over six sprints. In Sprint 1 you laid the foundation: Clean Architecture, a rich domain model, JWT identity, and the Categories module. In this sprint, you transform the project into a **use-case-driven** system: every operation becomes a Command or Query routed through **MediatR**, you build the **Campaigns** module with optimistic concurrency control, replace exceptions in expected flow with the **Result Pattern**, and write your first serious suite of **unit tests**.

- **Duration:** 15 Days (07/11/2026 to 21/11/2026)
- **Stand-up 1 (Day 5):** 11/11/2026 — Session Leader: **Asma ELhadidy**
- **Stand-up 2 (Day 10):** 16/11/2026 — Session Leader: **Kareem Zein**
- **Closing & Deadline (Day 15):** 21/11/2026 — Session Leader: **Mohamed Atef**
- **Code Review & Corrections (Days 16–18):** 22/11/2026 to 24/11/2026
- **Evaluation:** 100 Points
**Target Framework:** .NET 10 (`net10.0`) — fully compatible with .NET 8 and .NET 9. We continue on the same `.slnx` solution from Sprint 1 with SQL Server and thin Controllers.

Transform DonationHub into a use-case-driven system by migrating **all** endpoints to the **CQRS** pattern using **MediatR**. Implement the **Campaigns** module with optimistic concurrency control (Optimistic Concurrency), replace exception-driven business flow with the **Result Pattern**, enforce automatic input validation via MediatR Pipeline Behaviors, standardize all API errors using **RFC 9457 ProblemDetails** with `IExceptionHandler`, and establish a robust test suite of **at least 15 unit tests** using xUnit, Moq, and FluentAssertions.
Request journey after this sprint:

briefBlocks.code:
HTTP Request
     ↓
Thin Controller (Maps incoming HTTP request to Command or Query)
     ↓
MediatR Send
     ↓
Pipeline Behaviors (ValidationBehavior via FluentValidation)
     ↓
Command / Query Handler
     ↓
Domain Invariants & Concurrency Check (RowVersion)
     ↓
Result<T> (Success or Expected Domain Error from Catalogue)
     ↓
HTTP Response (or ProblemDetails on Failure)

briefBlocks.markdown: Before starting, make sure you thoroughly understand the following two concepts:

briefBlocks.text: 1. The CQRS Architectural Mindset & Vertical Slices

briefBlocks.markdown: Understand the fundamental difference between **Commands** (mutate state and have side effects) and **Queries** (pure reads without side effects). Understand why grouping related artifacts (Command + Handler + DTO + Validator) inside a **single feature slice (Feature Slice)** is superior to bloated monolithic Service classes.

Understand how ASP.NET Core signals client disconnection (`HttpContext.RequestAborted`), and how passing this token down to database calls prevents "orphaned" queries from continuing execution when no one is waiting for their result.
Resources for both concepts are included in Tasks 1 and 2 below — watch the primary ⭐ video for each before writing any code.
To ensure reproducibility, avoid commercial licensing pitfalls, and prevent breaking changes, **all teams** must adhere to the following pinned versions:

| Package / Tool | Pinned Version | Rationale & Guidance |
|---|---|---|
| **MediatR** | `[12.5.0]` | `<PackageReference Include="MediatR" Version="[12.5.0]" />` — Brackets prevent automatic upgrade to commercial v13+. |
| **FluentAssertions** | `[7.0.0]` | Apache 2.0 license. v8+ is commercial. (Acceptable alternative: Shouldly). |
| **Moq** | `[4.18.4]` | Avoids SponsorLink controversy present in 4.20. (Acceptable alternative: NSubstitute). |
| **RFC 9457 ProblemDetails** | Built-in | `builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();` paired with `IExceptionHandler`. |
| **Time Provider** | `TimeProvider` | Disallow direct `DateTime.UtcNow` in Handlers and Domain to ensure unit tests are deterministic. |

Running `dotnet add package` without `--version` fetches the latest version, so always inspect your `.csproj` file afterward.
All tasks below are **CORE** unless marked BONUS.

📘 **Written references:** Links marked 📘 point to the free [.NET Web API Zero to Hero](https://codewithmukesh.com/courses/dotnet-webapi-zero-to-hero/) course (.NET 10 articles + source code). Its samples use **PostgreSQL** and **Minimal APIs** — apply the ideas to our setup: **SQL Server** + **thin Controllers**, and always adhere to the pinned versions above (MediatR `[12.5.0]`, FluentAssertions `[7.0.0]`, Moq `[4.18.4]`) even if an article installs a newer one.
Migrate all previous endpoints (Identity and Categories), and implement upcoming Campaign endpoints, using CQRS:

items: Rewrite **every Sprint 1 use case** (IDN-01 to IDN-12, CAT-01 to CAT-04) as a Command or Query, each in its own feature slice (Command/Query + Handler + Validator + DTOs).
Create `IRequest<Result<T>>` definitions for all Commands and Queries.
Implement an isolated `IRequestHandler<TRequest, TResponse>` class for each individual use case.

Keep Controllers **extremely thin**: their sole responsibility is binding HTTP inputs, dispatching through `_mediator.Send()`, and mapping `Result<T>` to HTTP status codes (`Ok`, `Created` with `Location` header, `NoContent`) or to ProblemDetails on failure (see Task 6).

**Read/write split (SRS 3.3 rule 5):** Commands persist through the Generic Repository and Unit of Work. Queries may read directly from `DbContext` with `AsNoTracking()` and project to DTOs with `.Select()`.

briefBlocks.markdown: **Explain this decision in your README:** why do writes go through Repository/UoW while reads bypass it? This is an expected question in the explanation portion (20 points).

briefBlocks.text: Task 3 — Optimistic Concurrency Control (RowVersion on Campaign)

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement SRS requirement **CMP-10**:

items: Prevent "Lost Updates" when two users edit the same campaign at the same time.
Add `byte[] RowVersion` on `Campaign` and configure it as a concurrency token via Fluent API.
When concurrent edits occur, EF Core throws `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`. Catch it and return `Campaign.ConcurrencyConflict` (HTTP 409 Conflict) from the error catalogue.

briefBlocks.markdown: The client sends the last `RowVersion` it received with the `PUT /campaigns/{id}` update request. If the row has changed in the database since then, the second edit fails with 409 instead of silently overwriting the first edit.

briefBlocks.markdown: Eliminate throwing exceptions for **expected** failures (business rules and validation). Exceptions remain strictly for unexpected failures.

items: Implement the `Error` record with fields (`Code`, `Message`, `Type`), where `Type` is an enum named `ErrorType`.
Implement `Result` and `Result<T>` with factory methods (`Success`, `Failure`).
Map every `ErrorType` value to an HTTP status code according to the table below (SRS §6.1).
Define the **full** DonationHub error catalogue (SRS §6.1) as static errors **now**. Codes marked with a later sprint are declared now and used when that module arrives.

| `ErrorType` | HTTP Status |
|---|---|
| `Validation` | 400 Bad Request |
| `Unauthorized` | 401 Unauthorized |
| `Forbidden` | 403 Forbidden |
| `NotFound` | 404 Not Found |
| `Conflict` | 409 Conflict |
| `PayloadTooLarge` | 413 Payload Too Large (used by `File.TooLarge` from Sprint 4) |
| `UnprocessableEntity` | 422 Unprocessable Entity |
| `TooManyRequests` | 429 Too Many Requests |
| `Failure` | 500 Internal Server Error |

| `Auth.EmailAlreadyExists` | 409 Conflict | Registration with an existing email | Sprint 2 (Identity rewrite) |
| `Auth.RefreshTokenInvalid` | 401 Unauthorized | Refresh token unknown, expired, or revoked | Sprint 2 (Identity rewrite) |

| `Category.NotFound` | 404 Not Found | Specified category does not exist | Sprint 2 |

| `Campaign.EndDateInPast` | 422 Unprocessable | End date must be in the future | Sprint 2 |
| `Campaign.ConcurrencyConflict` | 409 Conflict | Concurrent update conflict detected | Sprint 2 |
| `Donation.NotFound` | 404 Not Found | Donation not found or not owned by you | Sprint 3 |
| `Donation.AmountOutOfRange` | 422 Unprocessable | Amount outside `DonationOptions` range | Sprint 3 |

briefBlocks.text: Task 5 — Automatic Validation via MediatR Pipeline Behavior

items: Implement `ValidationBehavior<TRequest, TResponse> : IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>`.
Collect all `IValidator<TRequest>` registered for the Command/Query and execute them **before** reaching the Handler.

If validation fails, short-circuit the pipeline immediately and return `Result.Failure` with code `Validation.Failed` and a dictionary of field-level errors (surfaced in the `errors` field inside ProblemDetails — see Task 6).
Write a Validator for **every** Command and Query that has inputs (SRS §6.2).

briefBlocks.markdown: **Separation of responsibilities:** Handlers **never repeat** basic input validation (empty? too long? email format?), while business rules (goal below raised, campaign in final state...) stay in the **Domain**.

briefBlocks.text: Task 6 — Global Exception Handling & RFC 9457 ProblemDetails

items: Implement `IExceptionHandler` (.NET 8+) to catch unexpected server crashes (500 Internal Server Error).

Log the exception with its full stack trace securely, and return to the client a **sanitized** RFC 9457 `ProblemDetails` response containing `traceId`, `title`, and a generic message without exposing any internal infrastructure details.
**All** errors (expected `Result` failures and unexpected exceptions) are returned as ProblemDetails (`application/problem+json`) with the extra fields required by SRS §6.1:
`code` — the catalogue code (e.g., `Campaign.NotFound`).
`traceId` — the request correlation id.
`errors` — for validation failures only: a field → messages dictionary.
The HTTP status code comes from the `ErrorType` mapping in Task 4.

briefBlocks.markdown: Example of an error response:

briefBlocks.code:
{
  "type": "https://httpstatuses.io/422",
  "title": "Goal amount cannot be lower than the raised amount.",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "Campaign.GoalBelowRaised",
  "traceId": "00-9f2d…"
}

briefBlocks.markdown: Never include `exception.Message` or the stack trace in a 500 response — they could leak table names, connection strings, or server paths. Those details belong strictly in the logs.

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement campaign features according to SRS §5.3:

items: **CMP-01:** Create Campaign `POST /campaigns` (bilingual Arabic and English title & description, `GoalAmount`, `EndDate`, `CategoryId`). Initial status is `Active` and `RaisedAmount = 0`. Returns `201 Created` with a `Location` header. Unknown category → `Category.NotFound`; `GoalAmount <= 0` → `Validation.Failed`; end date in the past → `Campaign.EndDateInPast`.

**CMP-02:** Update Campaign `PUT /campaigns/{id}` (titles, descriptions, category, end date, goal) enforcing domain invariants 2, 7, and 8: end date must be in the future (`Campaign.EndDateInPast`), goal cannot be lowered below `RaisedAmount` (`Campaign.GoalBelowRaised`), and a campaign in a final state (`Completed`, `Expired`) cannot be changed (`Campaign.NotActive`). The client sends the last `RowVersion` it received (see CMP-10).

**CMP-03:** Soft-delete Campaign `DELETE /campaigns/{id}` (`204 No Content`). Soft-deleted campaigns never appear in any query (Global Query Filter from Sprint 1). A campaign with donations is never hard-deleted (invariant 9).

**CMP-04:** Public list of active campaigns `GET /campaigns`, and public success stories `GET /campaigns/success-stories` (status `Completed`). (Pagination, filtering, and search come in Sprint 3 with CMP-08).

**CMP-05:** Campaign details `GET /campaigns/{id}` including all fields plus computed fields: `progressPercent` (min(100, (Raised/Goal)*100)) and `daysLeft` (computed from `TimeProvider`, never negative). Unknown id → `Campaign.NotFound`.
**CMP-06:** In Sprint 2, campaign creation and management is restricted to `Admin` (CampaignManager authorization comes in Sprint 3).
**CMP-10:** Concurrent edits are detected with `RowVersion` (Task 3); the second writer receives `Campaign.ConcurrencyConflict` (409).

**CMP-11:** Public endpoints (`GET /campaigns`, `GET /campaigns/success-stories`, `GET /campaigns/{id}`) return the title and description in the language of the `Accept-Language` header (`en` or `ar`), with fallback to `en` for any other or missing value. Admin endpoints return **both** languages (`TitleAr`, `TitleEn`, `DescriptionAr`, `DescriptionEn`).

Model the campaign as a rich entity: invariants live inside entity methods (e.g., `Campaign.Create(...)` and `Campaign.Update(...)`), not in Handlers. Implement the campaign-related domain invariants from SRS §4.5 (1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9).
Enums are returned as strings in JSON (e.g., `"status": "Active"`).

briefBlocks.markdown:
**Domain invariants required here (SRS §4.5):**

- **1.** `GoalAmount > 0`.
- **2.** `EndDate` must be in the future on creation or when changing the end date.
- **6.** When `RaisedAmount >= GoalAmount` after a donation succeeds, the campaign becomes `Completed`.
- **7.** `GoalAmount` cannot be lowered below the current `RaisedAmount`.
- **8.** A final status (Completed, Expired) cannot be changed.
- **9.** A campaign with donations is never hard-deleted; use soft delete.

| Method | Path | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/campaigns` | Anonymous |
| `GET` | `/campaigns/success-stories` | Anonymous |
| `GET` | `/campaigns/{id}` | Anonymous |
| `POST` | `/campaigns` | Admin |
| `PUT` | `/campaigns/{id}` | Admin |
| `DELETE` | `/campaigns/{id}` | Admin |

**About CMP-11:** Resource-file localization (`IStringLocalizer`, `.resx`) for messages arrives in Sprint 3, but **selecting data fields by language is required now**: fields are stored in two columns (Ar and En) and you choose which one to return.
All routes are under the `api/v1` prefix as in Sprint 1 (e.g., `/api/v1/campaigns`). Never return the `Campaign` entity itself from any endpoint — DTOs only.

Create a unit test project (`DonationHub.UnitTests`, or split it into `DonationHub.Domain.UnitTests` and `DonationHub.Application.UnitTests`). Write **at least 15 comprehensive unit tests** following the **Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA)** pattern. Use Moq `[4.18.4]` to fake Repositories, Unit of Work, and `TimeProvider` (or `FakeTimeProvider`), and FluentAssertions `[7.0.0]` for readable assertions. **Do not** test getters or EF Core itself.
**Suggested coverage:**

items: **1.** Domain invariant: Goal amount must be greater than zero.
**2.** Domain invariant: End date cannot be in the past (verified using a faked `TimeProvider`).
**3.** Domain invariant: Goal cannot be updated below raised amount (`Campaign.GoalBelowRaised`).
**4.** Domain invariant: A campaign in a final state (`Completed` / `Expired`) cannot be updated.
**5.** Calculation: `progressPercent` capped at 100%.
**6.** Calculation: `daysLeft` computed accurately relative to `TimeProvider` and never negative.
**7.** State transition: Campaign automatically transitions to `Completed` when the goal is reached.
**8.** Category rule: Deleting a category that has campaigns returns `Category.HasCampaigns`.
**9.** Validator: `CreateCampaignCommandValidator` rejects missing bilingual titles, `GoalAmount <= 0`, and an empty `CategoryId`.
**10.** Validator: Register command rejects a password that breaks the policy (8+ chars, uppercase, lowercase, digit).
**11.** Handler: `CreateCampaignCommandHandler` returns `Category.NotFound` when the category does not exist (faked Repository) and never calls `SaveChangesAsync`.
**12.** Handler: `CreateCampaignCommandHandler` adds the campaign and calls `IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync` once on success.
**13.** Handler: `UpdateCampaignCommandHandler` returns `Campaign.NotFound` for an unknown id.
**14.** Handler: `UpdateCampaignCommandHandler` maps a `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` to `Campaign.ConcurrencyConflict`.
**15.** Pipeline: `ValidationBehavior` short-circuits with `Validation.Failed` and never invokes the Handler when any Validator fails.
**16.** Handler: Login returns the same `Auth.InvalidCredentials` error for an unknown email and a wrong password (IDN-12).

solutionBlocks.markdown: This reference solution builds on the **exact same codebase** from the Sprint 1 reference solution (the same entity and interface names: `Campaign`, `IUnitOfWork`, `IReadDbContext`, `TimeProvider`...). The goal is not to copy it verbatim, but to understand the **why** behind each decision: why return a value instead of throwing an exception, why the Handler does not validate input format, and why we set `OriginalValue` for `RowVersion`.

To keep the length manageable, we show the key parts in full (Result, ValidationBehavior, error handling, Campaign slices, and tests), while repetitive slices (such as `UpdateCategory`, `Refresh`, `Logout`, and `CreateStaff`) follow the exact same pattern and are omitted. All code is written for .NET 10 with MediatR `[12.5.0]`, FluentAssertions `[7.0.0]`, and Moq `[4.18.4]`.

The tasks are interconnected, so the right order saves you from rewriting: **(4)** Result and Error first since everything depends on them → **(5)** ValidationBehavior → **(6)** mapping errors to ProblemDetails → **(1)** migrating Sprint 1 slices to MediatR → **(7)** Campaigns module alongside **(2)** and **(3)** → **(8)** tests (ideally written in parallel with each slice).

**Why?** Exceptions are expensive, hidden from the method signature (you cannot tell from `Task<Campaign>` that it might "fail" with `Campaign.NotFound`), and here they are used for control flow. With `Result<T>`, failure becomes **part of the return type**, forcing the caller to handle it and making testing a simple value comparison. We place `Error` and `Result` in `Domain/Common` (as suggested by SRS §3.4) because entity methods themselves will return `Result`.

Implicit conversions (implicit operators) make the code read naturally: `return CampaignErrors.NotFound;` or `return response;` inside a method returning `Result<T>`. **Important exception:** if `T` is an interface (such as `IReadOnlyList<CampaignSummaryResponse>`), C# does not apply user-defined implicit conversions in certain cases — use `Result<...>.Success(items)` explicitly.
The entire catalogue in a single file. Keeping it in one place prevents inventing ad-hoc codes across Handlers and turns the codes into a **stable contract** with the frontend:

**About `ErrorType.PayloadTooLarge`:** It is the ninth type in the task table (SRS §6.1), used only by `File.TooLarge` (413). As for `Server.Error`: it is an extra code solely for 500s, while the minimum catalogue (20 codes) is complete.

Delete the old `AppException`, `AppExceptionHandler`, and `AuthErrors`/`CategoryErrors` from Sprint 1 after migration — having two error systems side by side confuses reviewers and fails the "zero business exceptions" criterion. Move the `Roles` class (previously in the same `AppException.cs` file) to its own file `Application/Common/Roles.cs` before deleting. Watch out: after removing `AppExceptionHandler`, nothing maps the remaining `DomainException` in `Category`, `Money`, and `Donation` to 400/422 — it would become 500. Therefore, Validators must cover the CAT-02 rules (name required, 100 chars max) so the entity only throws in case of a programming bug.

**Why a Pipeline Behavior?** Because validation is a "cross-cutting concern": if you put it inside every Handler, you will repeat it 25 times and forget it once. The Behavior wraps **every** request flowing through MediatR, ensuring the Handler never receives invalid input.

**Verify this detail:** The constraint `where TResponse : IResultFactory<TResponse>` relies on the .NET DI container **skipping** open generics whose type constraints are not satisfied when resolving `IEnumerable<IPipelineBehavior<,>>` (which is what MediatR does). All our requests return `Result`/`Result<T>`, so this issue never occurs anyway. Also note that `RequestHandlerDelegate` in MediatR 12.5.0 accepts a `CancellationToken`, so we write `next(cancellationToken)`.
Registration in the Application layer — MediatR scans the assembly and registers all Handlers, and FluentValidation registers all Validators:

solutionBlocks.markdown: The `12.*` version for FluentValidation is just an example (the library is free under the Apache 2.0 license and was not pinned in the sprint table). It is best to let `dotnet add package` write the exact current version.

Example Validator — validates the **shape** of inputs only. Notice it does **not** check that `EndDate` is in the future: that is a domain rule (422) belonging in `Campaign.Create`, and it requires "current time" from `TimeProvider`:

**The dividing line:** The Validator answers "Is the request well-formed?" (400). The Domain answers "Is this allowed right now given the current state?" (409/422). If you need the database or the current time to decide, it usually does not belong in the Validator.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 6 — ProblemDetails for Expected and Unexpected Errors

solutionBlocks.markdown: We have two error paths and both must produce **the exact same format**: (1) an expected `Result` failure mapped by the Controller to ProblemDetails, and (2) an unexpected exception caught by `IExceptionHandler`. We add `traceId` centrally via `CustomizeProblemDetails` so it appears in **every** error response, including framework-generated errors (401 from JWT, or malformed JSON).
And `Program.cs` after this sprint:

`TryAdd` means any real catalogue `code` (set by `ProblemFrom`) **is never overwritten**. The fallback codes (`Auth.Unauthorized`, `Common.NotFound`...) are not part of the minimum catalogue, but rather handle errors generated by the framework itself — document them in the README. Verify in practice: send `POST /api/v1/campaigns` without a token, and you should see ProblemDetails with `code` and `traceId`.
Middleware ordering matters: `UseExceptionHandler()` must be **first** so it catches exceptions from everything downstream.

Each use case = one small file or folder containing the request, Handler, and Validator. When editing "Login", you open a single folder rather than touching a 400-line `AuthService` serving 7 cases. The Controller knows nothing except: bind → send → map result.

**Identity after migration.** In Sprint 1, the rules (IDN-10, IDN-12) lived inside `AuthService` in Infrastructure. Now we move the **decision** into a testable Handler, leaving Infrastructure with only technical details (`UserManager`, token storage) behind small interfaces — because `ApplicationUser` lives in Infrastructure and is invisible to Application. Practically, `IAuthService`/`AuthService` from Sprint 1 are replaced by two implementations in Infrastructure: `IdentityService` (wrapping `UserManager`) and `TokenService` (reusing `JwtTokenService`, `RefreshTokenGenerator`, and rotation logic), and their registration in `AddInfrastructureServices` changes accordingly:

`UserManager<T>` does not accept a `CancellationToken` in methods like `FindByEmailAsync` and `CheckPasswordAsync`, so the Infrastructure implementation accepts the token on the interface but cannot forward it to those calls. That is acceptable — what matters is that every direct EF Core call (such as the `RefreshTokens` table) receives the token. Furthermore, a failed `CreateAsync` result (such as violating the password policy) is converted into a `ValidationError` rather than an exception.

A write slice for Categories — notice the check via `AnyIncludingDeletedAsync`, a small method we added to `IGenericRepository<T>` (implementation: `_set.IgnoreQueryFilters().AnyAsync(predicate, ct)`), because soft-deleted campaigns are still database rows whose FK prevents deletion, and checking through the Repository is easy to mock in tests. Meanwhile, the decision stays in the Domain: `Category.EnsureCanBeDeleted` from Sprint 1 now returns `Result` instead of throwing:
A read slice — bypasses the Repository and projects directly:

We inject `ISender` rather than `IMediator`: the Controller only needs to send requests, and `ISender` is narrower (Interface Segregation Principle). **Ready-to-use README phrasing:** "Writes go through Repository + UoW so all changes stay within a single transaction, go through entity invariants, and remain easy to mock; reads do not mutate state, so they use `AsNoTracking` and direct projection to a DTO to fetch only the required columns without change-tracking overhead."

**CancellationToken:** ASP.NET Core automatically binds a `CancellationToken` in action parameters to `HttpContext.RequestAborted`. If the user closes the page, the token is cancelled, so EF Core aborts the query instead of completing it and consuming a connection from the pool for a result nobody will read. The chain must remain **unbroken** — a single missing link breaks it:

solutionBlocks.code:
Controller action (CancellationToken ct)        ← bound automatically to RequestAborted
  → sender.Send(command, ct)
    → ValidationBehavior: validator.ValidateAsync(context, ct) then next(ct)
      → Handler.Handle(request, ct)
        → uow.Repository<T>().GetByIdAsync(id, ct)  → FirstOrDefaultAsync(..., ct)
        → uow.SaveChangesAsync(ct)                   → db.SaveChangesAsync(ct)
        → read.Campaigns....ToListAsync(ct)

solutionBlocks.markdown: **TimeProvider:** Already registered since Sprint 1 as `services.AddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);`. The rule: the Handler reads the time **once** and passes it to the Domain as `DateTime utcNow`, keeping the Domain pure with zero dependencies:

**Common mistakes:** (1) Passing `CancellationToken.None` or `default` mid-chain. (2) Forgetting the token in `ToListAsync()` because the parameter is optional so the compiler won't warn you. (3) Calling `GetUtcNow()` multiple times within the same operation and getting slightly different timestamps — read it once.

A cancellation exception (`OperationCanceledException`) is not a bug: that is why we handled it in `GlobalExceptionHandler` with an Information log instead of Error, so the logs do not fill up with false errors whenever a user closes their browser.

**How does it work?** A SQL Server `rowversion` column updates automatically on every UPDATE. When saving, EF Core generates: `UPDATE ... WHERE Id = @id AND RowVersion = @original`. If someone else modified the row, the `RowVersion` condition matches 0 rows, so EF sees 0 affected rows and throws `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`.

**The subtle point:** In an API, the entity is reloaded on every request, so it holds the **current** `RowVersion` from the database, not what the user saw. We must set the value sent by the client in **`OriginalValue`** — that is what goes into the `WHERE` clause. For this reason, we added a small method to `IUnitOfWork`:

**The most common mistake:** Modifying `campaign.RowVersion` (the current value) instead of `OriginalValue` — no check occurs and the second edit silently succeeds. Test it manually: send two `PUT` requests with the same `rowVersion`; the first must return 200 and the second **409**.

`byte[]` is serialized in JSON as a Base64 string (such as `"AAAAAAAAB9E="`), and the client sends it back as-is. After `SaveChangesAsync`, EF Core reads the new value automatically generated by SQL Server, and we return it in the response so the client can use it on its next edit.

The `Campaign` entity from Sprint 1 used to throw `DomainException`. Now `Create` and `Update` return `Result` — the exact same rules, just as values. We also treated an active campaign whose **end date has actually passed** (before the background job in Sprint 4 runs) as non-editable:
Derived calculations are pure functions in the Domain — no database and no clock, so testing them is a one-liner:
Language selection (CMP-11). Small and isolated logic — in Sprint 3 it will be replaced by `RequestLocalization`:
**CMP-01** — Creation. Check order: category first (requires the database), then entity invariants, then saving:
**CMP-05 & CMP-11** — Details. The projection selects the language column inside SQL (`CASE WHEN`), and then we compute the derived fields in memory using the time from `TimeProvider`:
**CMP-04** — Public list. "Active" means `Active` **and** its end date has not yet passed. Success stories follow the same pattern with `Status == Completed`:
**CMP-03** — Soft delete. `Remove` turns into `UPDATE IsDeleted = 1` thanks to `SoftDeleteInterceptor` from Sprint 1, so invariant 9 is automatically protected:

**Why `ICurrentUser` instead of putting `CreatedByUserId` in the Command?** If it were in the request body, a client could send someone else's ID. User identity comes strictly from the token, never from the body.

**Verify this detail:** An `EndDate` arriving from JSON without `Z` comes in with `DateTimeKind.Unspecified`. Agree in the README that the API accepts dates in UTC format (such as `2026-12-31T00:00:00Z`), or normalize it in the Handler with `DateTime.SpecifyKind(..., DateTimeKind.Utc)` before passing it to the Domain.

**What do we test?** Things that contain a **decision**: entity invariants, calculations, Validators, and Handler branches (success/failure/conflict). **What do we NOT test?** Getters, EF Core itself, and thin Controllers. Thanks to `TimeProvider` and interfaces, every test here runs in milliseconds without a database.

**Why don't we test Query Handlers here?** Because `ToListAsync` and `FirstOrDefaultAsync` require an `IQueryable` that supports `IAsyncEnumerable` (i.e., real EF Core), and `List.AsQueryable()` throws an exception. Queries belong in integration tests against a real database (Testcontainers in a later sprint). That is also why we placed the calculations in the pure `CampaignCalculations` class and tested them directly.

Here there are 17 test methods (22 cases including `Theory` rows) covering all 16 suggested items. Name each test using the `Method_Scenario_ExpectedResult` format so a failure reads as a clear message on its own.

solutionBlocks.code:
## Sprint 2 — What was added
- CQRS with MediatR [12.5.0]: every use case is a command/query slice under `Application/Features`.
- `ValidationBehavior` (FluentValidation) runs before every handler.
- Result pattern + full error catalogue (`Domain/Common/ErrorCatalogue.cs`); no exceptions for expected failures.
- RFC 9457 ProblemDetails for all errors (`code`, `traceId`, `errors`); `GlobalExceptionHandler` for 500s.
- Campaigns module (CMP-01..06, 10, 11) with optimistic concurrency (`RowVersion`).
- 17 unit test methods (22 cases with theories): `dotnet test`

## Try it
1. Login as the seeded admin, create a category, then `POST /api/v1/campaigns` (dates in UTC, e.g. `2026-12-31T00:00:00Z`).
2. `GET /api/v1/campaigns/{id}` with header `Accept-Language: ar` → Arabic title/description.
3. Concurrency: send two `PUT /api/v1/campaigns/{id}` with the same `rowVersion` → the second returns 409 `Campaign.ConcurrencyConflict`.

## Design decisions
- **Writes vs reads:** commands use Generic Repository + Unit of Work (domain rules, one transaction, easy to mock);
  queries use `IReadDbContext` with `AsNoTracking()` and project straight to DTOs (no tracking cost, only needed columns).
- **Result instead of exceptions:** expected failures are part of the method signature and cheap to test; exceptions are for bugs and outages only.
- **Extra codes:** framework-level fallbacks `Auth.Unauthorized`, `Auth.Forbidden`, `Common.NotFound`, `Server.Error`.
- **Pinned packages:** MediatR [12.5.0], FluentAssertions [7.0.0], Moq [4.18.4] (newer versions are commercial or controversial).

items: Installing MediatR 13/14 or FluentAssertions 8 (from an article or `dotnet add package` without a version) — a direct violation of the pinned package versions table.
A Controller containing `if (request.GoalAmount <= 0)` or catching exceptions — all of this belongs in the Validator, Domain, or Handler.
A Handler repeating Validator checks (`string.IsNullOrEmpty(...)`), or a Validator containing a business rule that requires current time or the database.
Setting `RowVersion` as the current value instead of `OriginalValue` — the conflict is never detected and the second request succeeds.
A forgotten `DateTime.UtcNow` in a Handler or entity (search the entire solution before submitting).
`CancellationToken` accepted in the Controller but not forwarded to `Send` or `ToListAsync`.
A 401/403 or malformed JSON response without ProblemDetails or without `code`/`traceId`.
A 500 response containing `exception.Message` or the stack trace.
Returning the `Campaign` entity from the API, or returning both languages on public endpoints (CMP-11).
The public list returning an `Active` campaign whose end date has passed because the filter checks `Status` only.
Tests that test EF Core or getters, or rely on the real system clock and fail intermittently (Flaky).
Leaving `AppException` from Sprint 1 alongside the Result Pattern.

solutionBlocks.text: Questions to Prepare For in Review

items: Why do writes go through Repository/UoW while reads bypass it? What price do we pay for that?
What is the difference between a Command and a Query? Can a Command return a value? (Yes — such as a DTO after creation — but it must never be used for pure reads).
When do you use an exception vs. when do you use `Result`? What are the drawbacks of the Result Pattern (verbosity, ease of ignoring `IsFailure`)?
What happens exactly on `Send`? In what order do Pipeline Behaviors execute, and how does `ValidationBehavior` short-circuit execution?
Explain optimistic concurrency: what does the SQL statement generated by EF Core look like, and why do we set `OriginalValue`? When would you prefer pessimistic locking?
Why pin MediatR to `[12.5.0]`? What are the alternatives if you wanted to drop it?
What happens to an in-flight query if the client closes the connection, with vs. without passing the token?
How do you test that `daysLeft` is never negative without waiting actual days?
Why is `traceId` important? How does the support team use it when a user sends a screenshot of a 500 error?

solutionBlocks.markdown: **CMP-12 (Cancelled status):** Add `Cancelled` to `CampaignStatus` and treat it as a final state in `IsFinal`. Cancellation is an entity method returning `Result` and does not allow cancelling from a final state. Watch out: cancelled campaigns must not appear in the public list or in success stories.
**CMP-13 (Specification):** Encapsulate filtering conditions in composable objects instead of a chain of `if` statements inside the Handler — very useful for CMP-08 in Sprint 3:

**Domain Events:** Do not make the Domain depend on MediatR. Define `IDomainEvent` in the Domain and collect events in a list inside `Entity` (such as `CampaignCompletedEvent` from `ApplySucceededDonation`), then publish them from Infrastructure after `SaveChangesAsync` via an adapter that wraps them in `INotification`.

**IDN-13 (Refresh Token Reuse):** If a **revoked** token arrives (not expired), that is an indicator of theft: follow the `ReplacedByTokenId` chain, revoke the entire token family, and return `Auth.RefreshTokenInvalid`. And **IDN-14** (change password and update profile) are two new slices `ChangePassword/` and `UpdateProfile/` following the exact same pattern as Login.

If your solution achieves the same **principles** — logic-free Controllers, errors as values from a single catalogue, automatic validation before every Handler, unified ProblemDetails with `code` and `traceId`, concurrency conflicts that are genuinely detected, and controllable time in tests — then you are ready for Sprint 3 (donations, owner-based authorization, caching, and localization) even if the details differ from this solution. 🎉
